description: A two-state control that applies its change the instant it's toggled — distinct from a checkbox, which marks a selection typically confirmed later.

mapping.note: Off → not checked, On → checked; aria-checked.
States: Default → default, Disabled → disabled, Loading → interaction="loading"

notes: Behaviour from the WAI-ARIA switch pattern: a native button with role="switch" and aria-checked. Tab focuses it; Space and Enter toggle it. Figma Value=On is checked.
Figma has no focus state; a 2px focus ring (var(--border-interactive-focus)) is added for keyboard users.
Figma has no label for Switch: give each one an accessible name with aria-label or aria-labelledby.

paragraphs: A two-state control that applies its change the instant it's toggled — distinct from a checkbox, which marks a selection typically confirmed later.

sections.heading: Anatomy
paragraphs: ① Track — the pill-shaped background the handle slides within.
② Handle — the circular thumb that slides from one side to the other to indicate state.
③ Inner icon — a real Icon instance inside the handle, swapping between On/Off glyphs as the state changes.

sections.heading: Variants & States
paragraphs: 12 variants total: Value(Off/On) × Interaction(Default/Disabled/Loading) × Size(Medium/Small). Grid below shows Value × Interaction at Size=Medium.

sections.heading: Properties & Content
paragraphs: Two sizes: Medium (default/general use) and Small (dense contexts). Inner icon content swaps between On/Off glyphs immediately as state changes, reinforcing the resulting state at a glance rather than relying on handle position alone.

sections.heading: Behaviour & Accessibility
paragraphs: Click/tap anywhere on the track toggles state, not just the handle. Keyboard: focusable, toggles via Space. Loading shows a pending indicator on the handle, distinct from Disabled. Implement with real switch semantics (role=switch, aria-checked), not a generic checkbox role. Label by what the setting controls ("Notifications"), not by its current state.

Resolved from the earlier pass: the inner-icon slot described as "optional, unverified" in this component's prior review is in fact present and real — every On/Off variant carries a live Icon instance inside the handle (visible above in the anatomy diagram and the variant grid), not just a documented possibility.
